notes.text: **Zohar I 142a (Toldot)** — דָבָר אַחֵר אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם עוֹז לוֹ בָךְ, עֹז, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמֵר, יְיָ עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן, בְּגִין דְּאִצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְבַּר נָשׁ דְּיִתְעַסָּק בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא לִשְׁמֵיהּ דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, דְּכָל מַאן דְּאִתְעַסָּק בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְלָא אִשְׁתַּדַּל לִשְׁמָהּ, טַב לֵיהּ דְּלָא אִתְבְּרֵי. — "Strength" is Torah: a person must labor in Torah for the sake of the Holy One's Name, and one who labors in it without striving for its sake would be better off uncreated. R. Elazar opens the blessings of Isaac with this, and the passage closes: יַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווּ לִשְׁמָא דְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. The whole os is built on this one Zohar, which returns in ¶4 and ¶7. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 84:6** — אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם עוֹז לוֹ בָךְ מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם — Fortunate is the one whose strength rests in You, with highways in their heart. The Zohar's second reading takes עוֹז as Torah and מְסִלּוֹת as the inner road along which a person raises up God; Rav Tzadok expounds both halves in ¶2. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 29:11** — ה' עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן ה' יְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ בַשָּׁלוֹם — Hashem will give strength to His people; Hashem will bless His people with peace. The Zohar uses this verse to show that עֹז means Torah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Berakhot 17a** — לָעוֹשִׂים לִשְׁמָהּ וְלֹא לָעוֹשִׂים שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ. וְכָל הָעוֹשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, נוֹחַ לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא — The verse praises those who act for its own sake, not those who act for another motive; and whoever acts for another motive would be better off had he never been created. Rava's saying, from the verse 'good understanding to all who do them' (Psalms 111:10). Rav Tzadok reads it as the Talmudic form of the Zohar's טַב לֵיהּ דְּלָא אִתְבְּרֵי. *Mafteach: found*

**Tosafot, Berakhot 17a, s.v. העושה שלא לשמה** — וא"ת האמר רב יהודה אמר רב פרק מקום שנהגו (פסחים ד' נ:) לעולם יעסוק אדם בתורה ובמצות אפי' שלא לשמה שמתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה וי"ל דהכא מיירי שאינו לומד אלא לקנתר חביריו והתם מיירי שלומד ע"מ שיכבדוהו — Tosafot ask how this fits Rav Yehudah's teaching to engage even for an ulterior motive, and answer that Berakhot means one who learns only to taunt others, while Pesachim means one who learns in order to be honored. This is the 'degraded' not-for-its-sake of [1.9]. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Berakhot 14a; correct: Berakhot 17a (Tosafot s.v. העושה שלא לשמה))*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Shoftim 1** (Rav Tzadok) — raises the same contradiction between 'whoever acts not for its sake, better he had not been created' and 'one should always engage even not for its sake' (Tosafot's question); there he resolves it through the Or Zarua's view that one is punished for the ulterior motive yet rewarded for the study, and applies it to teaching a student who is not yet worthy. *checked*

notes.anchor: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם בַּתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
notes.text: **Pesachim 50b** — דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם בְּתוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ בָּא לִשְׁמָהּ — A person should always engage in Torah and mitzvot even for an ulterior motive, since from that he will come to act for its own sake. This is the source Tosafot cite. The same saying appears at Sotah 22b, Sanhedrin 105b, Horayot 10b and Arakhin 16b. *Mafteach: found*

**Eruvin 13b** — שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל ... נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ: נוֹחַ לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא, עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁנִּבְרָא — יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו — After two and a half years of dispute they took a vote and concluded that it would have been better for man not to be created; now that he has been, let him examine his deeds. Rav Tzadok's point: the phrase נוֹחַ לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא describes humanity in general, so Berakhot 17a is not a special curse on the one who studies for a motive. The exception is the Jacob-like person who acts only for Heaven; for him creation was worthwhile. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Toldot Yaakov Yosef, Chukat 254** (Chassidus) — R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne also reads Berakhot 17a's 'better not created' together with Eruvin 13b's 'now that he was created', and from this reconciles it with 'one should always engage even not for its sake'. This is Rav Tzadok's own move in [1.10]–[1.17].
ושלא לשמה נוח לו שלא נברא, ועכשיו שנברא יעסוק גם שלא לשמה, שמתוך המאור שבה יחזור למוטב ויעסוק לשמה.

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Maharal, Netivot Olam, Netiv Ahavat Hashem 2:5** (Machshava) — Maharal explains Berakhot 17a by the purpose of creation: all creatures exist only for God's glory, so one whose act is not for its sake misses the reason he was created. This is close to Rav Tzadok's link between lishmah and תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה.
כי כל הנבראים לא נבראו רק בשביל כבוד הקב"ה ולפיכך אם עושה שלא לשמה מוטב לו שלא נברא

**Psalms 68:5 (via Zohar I 142a)** — סֹלּוּ לָרֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ; Zohar: מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם ... כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמֵר סוֹלוּ לָרוֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת ... דָּא הַהִיא אוֹרַיְיתָא, דְּאִיהוּ אִשְׁתַּדַּל בָּהּ לְאֲרָמָא לֵיהּ לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּלְמֶעְבַּד לֵיהּ חֲטִיבָא בְּעַלְמָא — 'Extol Him who rides the heavens'. The 'highways in the heart' are the Torah one labors in to lift up the Holy One and make Him the single object of praise in the world. *Mafteach: missing*

**Berakhot 6a** — דִּכְתִיב: אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ הַיּוֹם ... אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: אַתֶּם עֲשִׂיתוּנִי חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם, וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם — 'You made Me one unique entity in the world, and I will make you one unique entity'. The next line (6a) grounds this in שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ... ה' אֶחָד. Rav Tzadok sees in it the Zohar's לְמֶעְבַּד לֵיהּ חֲטִיבָא בְּעַלְמָא. *Mafteach: found*

**Deuteronomy 26:17** — אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ הַיּוֹם לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים — You have singled out Hashem today to be your God. The verse Berakhot 6a expounds. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Deuteronomy 26:16; correct: Deuteronomy 26:17)*

**Rosh Hashanah 4a** — וְהָתַנְיָא, הָאוֹמֵר: סֶלַע זוֹ לִצְדָקָה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיִּחְיוּ בָּנַי, וּבִשְׁבִיל שֶׁאֶזְכֶּה בָּהּ לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא — הֲרֵי זֶה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר. לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כָּאן בְּגוֹיִם — One who gives a coin to charity so that his children may live, or to earn the World to Come, is fully righteous. The Gemara resolves the conflict with Cyrus's case: here a Jew, there a gentile. Rav Tzadok explains why the same motive counts differently: the Jew's root desire is to do the Father's will. Pesachim 8a has the same baraita. *Mafteach: found*

**Rosh Hashanah 3b** — אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן קוֹדֶם שֶׁהֶחְמִיץ, כָּאן לְאַחַר שֶׁהֶחְמִיץ — Cyrus is praised before he soured and faulted after. The Gemara then (4a) objects that his offerings 'for the life of the king and his sons' (Ezra 6:10) should be meritorious, and answers with the Israel/gentile distinction of [2.9]. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Rosh Hashanah 3a; correct: Rosh Hashanah 3b)*

**Genesis 27:8** — וְעַתָּה בְנִי שְׁמַע בְּקֹלִי לַאֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מְצַוָּה אֹתָךְ — Now, my son, heed my voice in what I command you. Rav Tzadok reads Rebecca's 'command' as making Jacob's act a mitzvah of honoring his mother, so that his motive would be pure. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereishit Rabbah 65:15** — וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיִּקַּח וַיָּבֵא לְאִמּוֹ, אָנוּס וְכָפוּף וּבוֹכֶה — On Genesis 27:14: he went, took and brought them to his mother under compulsion, bent over and weeping. For Rav Tzadok this shows that Jacob felt no personal desire for the blessings and acted only to obey his mother. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: דְּיַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווֹ לִשְׁמֵיהּ דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
notes.text: **Zohar I 142a** — תָּא חֲזֵי, יַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווּ לִשְׁמָא דְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וּבְגִין כָּךְ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הֲוָה עִמֵּיהּ תָּדִיר, דְּלָא אַעֲדֵי מִנֵּיהּ שְׁכִינְתָּא — All of Jacob's deeds were for the Holy One's Name, so the Shekhinah never left him. Through the Shekhinah, Rebecca learned of Isaac's plan and told Jacob. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayishlach 6** (Rav Tzadok) — cites the same Zohar (I 142a). There it explains Jacob's efforts to gain wealth from Laban's flocks: he knew that everything comes from Hashem, so even his worldly effort was לשמא דקוב"ה. This is the worldly side of what ¶4 here calls the 'six blessings of this world'. *checked*

**Bereishit Rabbah 66:3** — רַבִּי אַחָא אָמַר יִתֶּן לְךָ וְיִתֶּן לְךָ אֱלָהוּתָא, אֵימָתַי לִכְשֶׁתִּצְטָרֵךְ לָהּ — R. Acha: 'May He give you' means He will give you Divinity, at the time you need it. The Midrash's example is Samson's last prayer. Rav Tzadok reads אֱלָהוּתָא as God's help in making one's inner intent purely for Heaven. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 8:1** (Rav Tzadok) — the same 'Divinity' (אלהותא) is the life from Hashem inside food and drink, 'what comes out of Hashem's mouth', which ties the blessing to the holiness of the Shabbat meals. **Peri Tzadik, Vayeshev 13:1** (Rav Tzadok) — reads אֱלֹהִים / אלהותא as gevurah, the power to conquer one's inclination, together with the Torah reading of מטל השמים. *checked*

**Genesis 27:29** — יַעַבְדוּךָ עַמִּים וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ לְאֻמִּים הֱוֵה גְבִיר לְאַחֶיךָ — Let peoples serve you and nations bow to you; be lord over your brothers. Rav Tzadok takes these as the six worldly blessings that follow the Torah blessings of v. 28. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 7:2** (Rav Tzadok) — counts the blessings as ten: the first ones (טל, שמני הארץ, דגן, תירוש) correspond to the upper attributes and the World to Come, then six blessings for the six workdays in which this world was created. There he also cites the Ari, that Shabbat eating is holy even when meant for bodily pleasure, and explains why ויתן לך is said on Motzaei Shabbat. *checked*

**Rambam, Hilkhot De'ot 3:3** — נִמְצָא הַמְהַלֵּךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זוֹ כָּל יָמָיו עוֹבֵד אֶת ה' תָּמִיד. אֲפִלּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן ... וְעַל עִנְיָן זֶה צִוּוּ חֲכָמִים וְאָמְרוּ וְכָל מַעֲשֶׂיךָ יִהְיוּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם — One who directs his bodily life toward knowing Hashem serves Him constantly, even in business and even in sleep. This is the meaning of 'let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven' (Avot 2:12). *Mafteach: missing*

**Shabbat 118a** — כָּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה' ... וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ — Whoever delights the Shabbat receives a boundless inheritance, Jacob's inheritance. Rav Tzadok notes the wording: one 'delights the Shabbat', not 'delights himself on Shabbat'. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Shavuot 5:1** (Rav Tzadok) — the same close reading, with the Ari's teaching that self-directed Shabbat pleasure is also holy, applied to the dispute over whether a festival must be wholly 'for Hashem' or partly 'for you'. **Peri Tzadik, Pinchas 18:2** (Rav Tzadok) — the same reading: pleasure on Shabbat is a mitzvah even for the body, but only intent for Heaven makes it give light, 'a lamp with no light' otherwise. *checked*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Aseret HaDibrot, Shabbat, Ner Mitzvah 76** (Musar / Kabbalah) — the Shelah makes the same point about the wording: the pleasure must be done for the honor of Shabbat, like a feast made for an honored guest, and not for one's own enjoyment.
ואמרו רז"ל כל המענג את השבת, ולא אמרו כל המענג בשבת, כי האדם לא יהיה כוונתו על עצמו לענג, רק יעשה העונג בשביל כבוד שבת

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Sefat Emet, Bamidbar 8:2** (Chassidus) — reports the same close reading from his grandfather, the Chiddushei HaRim. The reward comes to the one who sets aside his own will for Shabbat and rejoices in Hashem's salvation.
על אמרם המענג את השבת נותנין לו משאלות לבו. ולא אמרו המענג עצמו בשבת.

**The Arizal, on Shabbat eating** — Rav Tzadok cites without a place that whatever a Jew eats on Shabbat, even for his own enjoyment, is holy; in Rosh Chodesh Shvat 3 he gives it as אִיתָא מֵהָאֲרִ״י ... שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכֵל בְּשַׁבָּת, אַף לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ, הוּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה. The exact passage in the Arizal's writings was not found in Pri Etz Chaim, Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaKavanot or Sha'ar HaMitzvot as searched. The same teaching is quoted in his name by later Chassidus: **Shem MiShmuel, Beshalach 3** “אִיתָא בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ״י שֶׁמַּאֲכַל שַׁבָּת אֵינוֹ מְגַשֵּׁם”, and Korach and Ki Teitzei there. He states it in his own words in Toldot 7:2. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: "וַיֹּאמֶר רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ ה'
notes.text: **Genesis 27:27–28** — וַיֹּאמֶר רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה'. וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ — See, my son's scent is like the scent of a field Hashem has blessed; may God give you of the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth. The verses recited after Havdalah, which Rav Tzadok explains in the Motzaei Shabbat teaching that follows. *Mafteach: found*

**Shabbat 88a** — מַאי דִּכְתִיב כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר וְגוֹ' — לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתַפּוּחַ, לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֶם לְעָלָיו, אַף יִשְׂרָאֵל הִקְדִּימוּ נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע — Israel is likened to an apple tree, which puts out fruit before leaves, because at Sinai Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear'. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar II 88a (Yitro), on the Shabbat meals** — בֵּיהּ בְּלֵילְיָא, מִתְבָּרְכָא מַטְרוֹנִיתָא, וְכֻלְּהוּ חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין, וּמִתְבָּרְכָא פָּתוֹרֵיהּ דְּבַר נָשׁ, וְנִשְׁמְתָא אִתּוֹסְפַת — On Shabbat night the Matronita and the whole 'field of apples' are blessed, a person's table is blessed, and an added soul comes. Rav Tzadok gives no reference for the phrase. This Zohar passage pairs it with the additional soul, as he does in ¶6. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ta'anit 29b** — וַיֹּאמֶר רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה', אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִים — Rav: 'the scent of a blessed field' is the scent of an apple orchard. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Tzav 8:1** (Rav Tzadok) — builds the same chain: Ta'anit 29b's apple field, Bereishit Rabbah's 'scent of Gan Eden' entering with Jacob, Israel likened to apples at Sinai (Shabbat 88a), and the Shabbat additional soul by which Israel become תפוחין קדישין. It adds that Jacob's form resembled Adam's before the sin. *checked*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Likutei Halakhot, Choshen Mishpat, Hilkhot Arev 3:41** (Chassidus, Breslov) — R. Natan also explains the Motzaei Shabbat recitation of ויתן לך (Jacob's blessing, from which Esau was pushed out) and of ויהי נועם ... ומעשה ידינו כוננה. Both draw Shabbat's holiness onto the weekday labors so that the weekday 'doing' is sanctified.
וְעַל כֵּן אוֹמְרִים בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, "וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹקִים", שֶׁהִיא בִּרְכַּת יַעֲקֹב, שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִיִּצְחָק וְגֵרֵשׁ אֶת עֵשָֹו מִן הַבְּרָכָה

**Bereishit Rabbah 66:3** — דָּבָר אַחֵר, מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם, זוֹ מִקְרָא. וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ, זוֹ מִשְׁנָה. דָּגָן, זוֹ תַּלְמוּד. תִּירשׁ, זֶה אַגָּדָה — Dew of heaven is Scripture, richness of the earth is Mishnah, grain is Talmud, wine is Aggadah. Rav Tzadok uses this both in ¶4 (God's help toward lishmah even in Torah study) and here (Torah study carried into the weekdays). *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: שֶׁכָּל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
notes.text: **Avot 3:5** — רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה אוֹמֵר: כָּל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עֹל מַלְכוּת וְעֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ — Whoever accepts the yoke of Torah is relieved of the yoke of government and of worldly labor. Rav Tzadok reads 'let peoples serve you' (Genesis 27:29) as this relief. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: (חֵלֶק א, סב א; פג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)
notes.text: **Zohar I 62a (Noach)** — אֲתָא בַּר נָשׁ לְאִתְדַּכָּאָה, מְסַיְיעִין לֵיהּ בְּנִשְׁמְתָא קַדִּישָׁא וְדָכָאן לֵיהּ וּמְקַדְּשִׁין לֵיהּ וְאִקְרֵי קָדוֹשׁ — When a person comes to purify himself he is helped with a holy neshamah, purified and sanctified, and is called 'holy'. A person without it has only nefesh and ruach. Rav Tzadok's second address, “I 83, beginning of b”, is the passage on the person in whom the *neshamah* rules: כְּדֵין הַהוּא בַּר נָשׁ אִקְרֵי קָדוֹשׁ (Zohar, Lech Lecha, Sefaria 17:3, 8), which Sefaria's page division puts at the end of I 82b. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: "לֹא יָרֵעוּ וְלֹא יַשְׁחִיתוּ בְּכָל הַר קָדְשִׁי
notes.text: **Isaiah 11:9** — לֹא יָרֵעוּ וְלֹא יַשְׁחִיתוּ בְּכָל הַר קָדְשִׁי כִּי מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה אֶת ה' כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים — They will do no harm or destruction on all My holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of Hashem. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I 138a (Midrash HaNe'elam, Toldot)** — אֲבָל לָא מְנַוְולָה כְּקַדְמִיתָא לְמֶחֱטֵי בֵּיהּ. הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב, לֹא יָרֵעוּ וְלֹא יַשְׁחִיתוּ בְּכָל הַר קָדְשִׁי וְגו'. אָמַר רִבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הוּא לִבָּא דִּמְדוֹרֵיהּ דְּיִצֶּר הָרָע בֵּיהּ — The evil inclination will remain in the world (it is needed like rain) but no longer foul enough to cause sin. R. Shimon: 'My holy mountain' is the heart, where the inclination dwells. The printed reference קלא א is a misprint for קלח א; Rav Tzadok himself cites זח"א קלח א במה"נ in Terumah 1. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: הוּא לִבָּא דִּמְדוֹרֵיהּ דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע בֵּיהּ
notes.text: **Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Terumah 1:1** (Rav Tzadok) — the same derasha: on Shabbat Hashem dwells in each Jew's heart and the heart becomes הר קדשי (Isaiah 11:9 with Midrash HaNe'elam), so one is saved from the inclination's accusation. It adds that Torah scholars are like Shabbatot and have this state always. *checked*

notes.anchor: "שֹׁמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשֹׁמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע"
notes.text: **Isaiah 56:2** — אַשְׁרֵי אֱנוֹשׁ יַעֲשֶׂה זֹּאת ... שֹׁמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשֹׁמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע — Fortunate is one who keeps Shabbat from profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil. Rav Tzadok reads the second clause as the result of the first. *Mafteach: missing*

**Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaShabbat 1** (R. Chaim Vital, from the Arizal) — on the added soul of Shabbat that a person should keep into the week: וּבָזֶה יִכּוֹנוּ דְרָכָיו ... וּמֻבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא וְלֹא יָבוֹאוּ הַחֲטָאִים עַל יָדוֹ וְלֹא יְקַטְרֵג בּוֹ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע. Whoever directs his heart on Shabbat is assured that he will not sin and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. The parallel in **Sha'ar HaKavanot, Derushei Shabbat** (Sefaria: Sermons on the Order of the Sabbath 1:4) adds “nor make him sin all that week”, the point Rav Tzadok repeats in Rosh Chodesh Adar 7. *Mafteach: missing (now added)*

**Siddur, Weekday Ma'ariv, Atah Chonantanu (Motzaei Shabbat)** — אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ הָחֵל עָלֵינוּ הַיָּמִים הַבָּאִים לִקְרָאתֵנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם, חֲשׂוּכִים מִכָּל חֵטְא וּמְנֻקִּים מִכָּל עָוֹן וּמְדֻבָּקִים בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ — Begin the coming days for us in peace, kept from all sin, cleansed of all iniquity, and cleaving to Your awe. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ta'anit 8b** — וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שֶׁמֶשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת — צְדָקָה לַעֲנִיִּים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְזָרְחָה לָכֶם יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה וּמַרְפֵּא — Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, from the verse 'the sun of righteousness shall shine for you who fear My Name' (Malachi 3:20). Since the verse is read about Shabbat, those it addresses (יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי) are Israel on Shabbat. *Mafteach: missing*

**Yerushalmi Demai 4:1** — רִבִּי בִּיבִי בְשֵׁם רִבִּי חֲנִינָא אֵימַת שַׁבָּת עָלָיו וְהוּא אוֹמֵר אֱמֶת — An am ha'aretz may be trusted on Shabbat about tithing, since the awe of Shabbat is on him and he tells the truth. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: שַׁבָּת דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבַּתָּא אִיהִי יִרְאָה וְשַׁרְיָא בָהּ יִרְאָה
notes.text: **Zohar I 5b (Introduction)** — אַעֲבַר כָּרוֹזָא וְאָמַר, מִקְדָּשַׁי תִּירָאוּ, וְדָא שַׁבָּת דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבַּתָּא דְּאִיהִי יִרְאָה, וְשַׁרְיָא בָהּ יִרְאָה — 'You shall fear My sanctuary' (Leviticus 19:30) refers to the Shabbat of Friday evening, which is awe and in which awe dwells. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Terumah 13:3** (Rav Tzadok) — the same cluster: the prayer חשוכים מכל חטא ... ומדובקים ביראתך, the Yerushalmi's אימת שבת, Ta'anit 8b's יראי שמי, and מלוה מלכה from הפעם ילוה, all as drawing Shabbat's awe and holiness into the weekdays. It adds that the Havdalah wine turns that awe into joy (שמחתי מתוך יראתי). **Peri Tzadik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat 4:12** (Rav Tzadok) — the Motzaei Shabbat meal 'escorts the Queen' and is סעודתא דדוד מלכא, the one who raised up teshuvah. *checked*

**Genesis 29:34** — עַתָּה הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי אֵלַי כִּי יָלַדְתִּי לוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָנִים — Now my husband will become attached to me, for I have borne him three sons (on Levi's name). Rav Tzadok derives מְלַוֶּה from this sense of 'joining'. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar I 153b (Vayetzei)** — דְּהָא רְתִיכָא עִלָּאָה, אֲבָהָן וְדָוִד מַלְכָּא דְּאִתְחַבַּר בְּהוּ, וְכֻלְּהוּ אַרְבַּע אִינוּן רְתִיכִין עִלָּאִין, רָזָא דִשְׁמָא קַדִּישָׁא — The supernal chariot is the three Patriarchs with King David joined to them, four together. The same passage explains Leah's sons Reuben, Simeon, Levi, then Judah who inherited kingship. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 27:4** — אַחַת שָׁאַלְתִּי מֵאֵת ה' אוֹתָהּ אֲבַקֵּשׁ שִׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית ה' כָּל יְמֵי חַיַּי לַחֲזוֹת בְּנֹעַם ה' וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלוֹ — One thing I ask: to dwell in Hashem's house, to gaze on Hashem's pleasantness and to visit His sanctuary. Rav Tzadok reads the two halves as Shabbat's two gifts. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar II 88a–b (Yitro) and II 252b (Pekudei, Heikhalot)** — Yitro: תָּא חֲזֵי, בִּסְעוּדָתֵי אִלֵּין, אִשְׁתְּמוֹדְעוּן יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאִינּוּן בְּנִי מַלְכָּא ... וּמַאן דְּפָגִים חַד סְעוּדָתָא מִנַּיְיהוּ ... דְּלָאו מִבְּנֵי הֵיכָלָא דְּמַלְכָּא הוּא. Pekudei: כַּד עָיֵיל שַׁבְּתָא, מִתְסַדְּרָאן תַּמָּן כָּל פָּתוֹרֵי דִּבְנֵי עָלְמָא, דְּאִקְרוּ בְּנֵי הֵיכָלָא דְּמַלְכָּא — Through the three meals Israel are recognized as the King's children of His palace; whoever omits one shows he is not of them. The Yitro passage also calls the third meal סְעוּדָתָא דִּזְעֵיר אַפִּין, from which all six weekdays are blessed. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar II 223b; correct: Zohar II 252b (with II 88a–b))*

**Psalms 90:17** — וִיהִי נֹעַם אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהֵינוּ עָלֵינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָה עָלֵינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ כּוֹנְנֵהוּ — May the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us, and the work of our hands, establish it. Said on Motzaei Shabbat. Rav Tzadok reads the two 'work of our hands' clauses as weekday acts for Heaven and as acts that 'give strength' above. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: יָהֲבִין תּוּקְפָא וְחֵילָא לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
notes.text: **Zohar II 32b (Bo)** — דְּהָא כַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל עַבְדִין עוֹבָדִין דְּלָא כַּשְׁרָן, כִּבְיָכוֹל מַתִּישִׁין חֵילָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וְכַד עַבְדִין עוֹבָדִין דְּכַשְׁרָן, יַהֲבִין תּוּקְפָּא וְחֵילָא לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. וְעַל דָּא כְּתִיב, תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים — Unworthy deeds, as it were, weaken the Holy One's power; worthy deeds give Him strength, as 'give strength to God' (Psalms 68:35). This ties back to the עֹז of ¶1. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: וּבְגִין כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְפַרְנְסֵי לַאֲבִיהֶן שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם תָּנֵינַן
notes.text: **Zohar III 7b (Vayikra)** — וְעַל דָּא סְעוּדָתָא דְּמַלְכָּא אִתְעַכָּב, בְּגִין סְעוּדָתָא דְּעַבְדוֹהִי. וּבְגִין כַּךְ, יִשְׂרָאֵל מְפַרְנְסֵי לַאֲבִיהֶן שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם תָּנֵינָן — The King's meal waits on His servants' meal, the scent of the offering. So Israel 'sustain their Father in Heaven'. Rav Tzadok reads it as God's gratification that His will is done. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar III 4b; correct: Zohar III 7b)*

connector.why: Same chain for the apple field: Ta'anit 29b, Shabbat 88a, additional soul, חקל תפוחין; it is about the Shabbat-night meal, not lishmah or Motzaei Shabbat.
Shares Genesis 27:8 and some rare words; the opening paragraph is about the three meals and Isaac's matamim, not the lishmah theme.
Raises Tosafot's same contradiction (Berakhot 17a vs Pesachim 50b) and resolves it differently (Or Zarua).
Uses ויתן לך אלהותא and the mikra/mishnah reading of מטל השמים, applied to gevurah over the inclination.
Para 12 explains the Motzaei Shabbat meal as escorting the Queen, סעודתא דדוד מלכא (snippet read).
Ten blessings, six for this world; the Ari on Shabbat eating; why ויתן לך is said on Motzaei Shabbat.

candidates.why: It is the very passage Rav Tzadok cites (Zohar I 142a, R. Elazar on Psalms 84:6). Used as the source note, not as a separate parallel.

found.why: Reconciles Berakhot 17a with Pesachim 50b through Eruvin 13b's 'now that he was created', as Rav Tzadok does.
Explains 'better not created' by the purpose of creation (God's glory).

Same close reading, from the Chiddushei HaRim.
